description: HTTP front-end traffic through Trickster: request rates, status classes, latency, egress and client connections, plus backend health probes and upstream resilience (retries, mirrors, SRV origin resolution, SigV4).

panels.title: Requests/s
panels.description: Front-end HTTP requests per second that matched a backend route, whatever the outcome (served, cached, denied by an ACL or rate limit, rejected). Requests routed through an ALB, a rule or a mirror are counted again under each target backend's name, so totals across all backends overstate client traffic.

targets.expr: sum(rate(trickster_frontend_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}[$__rate_interval])) or vector(0)

panels.title: 5xx ratio
panels.description: Share of front-end responses in the 5xx class: origin errors relayed to clients plus 502/504 answers Trickster gives when the origin is unreachable or times out. Orange above 1%, red above 5%; break it down in the Requests row.

targets.expr: (sum(rate(trickster_frontend_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", http_status="5xx"}[$__rate_interval])) or vector(0)) / clamp_min((sum(rate(trickster_frontend_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}[$__rate_interval])) or vector(0)), 1e-9)

panels.title: 4xx ratio
panels.description: Share of front-end responses in the 4xx class: origin 4xx answers plus Trickster's own refusals (IP/geo ACL 403s, rate-limit 429s, authentication failures, max_query_range 400s). A sudden rise usually means a policy or a client change. Orange above 10%, red above 25%.

targets.expr: (sum(rate(trickster_frontend_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", http_status="4xx"}[$__rate_interval])) or vector(0)) / clamp_min((sum(rate(trickster_frontend_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}[$__rate_interval])) or vector(0)), 1e-9)

panels.title: Under 500 ms
panels.description: Share of front-end requests answered in 500 ms or less, end to end on Trickster's side including streaming the body. It is read straight from the 500 ms histogram bucket, so it is exact. 1xx responses (WebSocket and other upgrades, timed for the tunnel's lifetime) are excluded. Red below 90%, green from 95%; reads 'no traffic' when nothing was timed.

targets.expr: sum(rate(trickster_frontend_requests_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", http_status!="1xx", le="0.5"}[$__rate_interval])) / (sum(rate(trickster_frontend_requests_duration_seconds_count{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", http_status!="1xx"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0) or vector(-1)

panels.title: Mean latency
panels.description: Mean front-end response time (histogram sum / count), exact rather than bucket-estimated. Excludes 1xx upgrades; CONNECT requests are never timed. Long downloads raise it, so read it with the 500 ms share. Orange from 500 ms, red from 2 s; reads 'no traffic' when nothing was timed.

targets.expr: sum(rate(trickster_frontend_requests_duration_seconds_sum{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", http_status!="1xx"}[$__rate_interval])) / (sum(rate(trickster_frontend_requests_duration_seconds_count{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", http_status!="1xx"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0) or vector(-1)

panels.title: Egress
panels.description: Response body bytes per second written to clients, after compression and before TLS; headers are not counted. Tunnels and long streams add their bytes when they finish, which shows as spikes. ALB requests count their bytes under the ALB and again under the member.

targets.expr: sum(rate(trickster_frontend_written_bytes_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}[$__rate_interval])) or vector(0)

panels.title: Conn. limit used
panels.description: Worst instance's active connections divided by its connections_limit; reads 'no limit set' unless a listener sets connections_limit > 0. Above the limit, new connections wait in the accept backlog. Process-wide (ignores Backend). TLS connections are never subtracted when they close, so on HTTPS listeners this climbs over the process lifetime.

targets.expr: max(trickster_proxy_active_connections{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"} / (trickster_proxy_max_connections{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"} > 0)) or vector(-1)

panels.title: Retry ratio
panels.description: Upstream retry attempts per front-end request, across all routes in scope. Reads 0 unless a path has a retry block; a request retried twice adds two. Orange above 1%, red above 5%; the per-path ratio is in the Upstream resilience row.

targets.expr: (sum(rate(trickster_proxy_upstream_retries_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}[$__rate_interval])) or vector(0)) / clamp_min((sum(rate(trickster_frontend_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}[$__rate_interval])) or vector(0)), 1e-9)

panels.title: Requests/s by backend
panels.description: Front-end requests per second for the 10 busiest backends in scope. An ALB appears under its own name and its members appear again under theirs, as do rule targets and mirror backends receiving copies. Native SQL wire listeners (MySQL, PostgreSQL) are not HTTP and never appear here.

targets.expr: topk(10, sum by (backend_name) (rate(trickster_frontend_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Requests/s by status class
panels.description: Front-end requests per second by the status class Trickster wrote to the client (2xx, 3xx, 4xx, 5xx; 1xx is WebSocket and other upgrades, 0xx an out-of-range code). Only the class is recorded; exact origin codes for cached routes are on the Caching dashboard. A request that wrote nothing (client gave up first) is recorded as 2xx.

targets.expr: sum by (http_status) (rate(trickster_frontend_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Share by backend (range)
panels.description: The 10 busiest backends' share of front-end requests. Requests routed through an ALB, a rule or a mirror are counted again under each target backend's name. Totals cover the dashboard's time range; hover a slice for its count.

targets.expr: sort_desc(topk(10, sum by (backend_name) (increase(trickster_frontend_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}[$__range]))) > 0)

panels.title: Share by provider (range)
panels.description: Front-end requests by backend provider (reverseproxy, prometheus, alb, clickhouse...). Requests routed through an ALB, a rule or a mirror are counted again under each target backend's name. Totals cover the dashboard's time range; hover a slice for its count.

targets.expr: sort_desc(sum by (provider) (increase(trickster_frontend_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}[$__range])) > 0)

panels.title: Share by status (range)
panels.description: Front-end requests by the status class written to the client. A request that wrote nothing (client gave up first) is recorded as 2xx. Totals cover the dashboard's time range; hover a slice for its count.

targets.expr: sort_desc(sum by (http_status) (increase(trickster_frontend_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}[$__range])) > 0)

panels.title: Share by method (range)
panels.description: Front-end requests by HTTP method. Totals cover the dashboard's time range; hover a slice for its count.

targets.expr: sort_desc(sum by (method) (increase(trickster_frontend_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}[$__range])) > 0)

panels.title: 5xx ratio by backend
panels.description: Share of each backend's front-end responses in the 5xx class, for the 10 worst backends. A backend with no line has served no 5xx since Trickster started. Dashed lines mark 1% and 5%. An ALB's ratio reflects the members it picked; check the member backends' lines too.

targets.expr: topk(10, sum by (backend_name) (rate(trickster_frontend_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", http_status="5xx"}[$__rate_interval])) / (sum by (backend_name) (rate(trickster_frontend_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0))

panels.title: 4xx ratio by backend
panels.description: Share of each backend's front-end responses in the 4xx class, for the 10 worst backends. Includes origin 4xx answers and Trickster's own refusals: ACL 403s, rate-limit 429s, authentication failures and max_query_range 400s. The Access Control dashboard shows which policy denied a request.

links.title: Access Control & Rate Limiting: denials by policy

targets.expr: topk(10, sum by (backend_name) (rate(trickster_frontend_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", http_status="4xx"}[$__rate_interval])) / (sum by (backend_name) (rate(trickster_frontend_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0))

panels.title: Requests/s by method
panels.description: Front-end requests per second by client method, as received (QUERY stays QUERY even when the route forwards it as POST). A method that no path of the backend accepts matches no route and is not counted.

targets.expr: sum by (method) (rate(trickster_frontend_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Non-2xx requests/s by backend and status class
panels.description: Front-end requests per second that did not get a 2xx, by backend and status class, so errors and redirects are not hidden under the success traffic. Ratios are in the panels above; the routes behind them are in Top error routes (range).

targets.expr: sum by (backend_name, http_status) (rate(trickster_frontend_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", http_status!="2xx"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Top error routes (range)
panels.description: The 10 routes (status class, backend, method, configured path) that returned the most 4xx and 5xx responses over the dashboard's time range. A 4xx can be an ACL or rate-limit denial as well as an origin error.

targets.expr: sort_desc(topk(10, sum by (http_status, backend_name, method, path) (increase(trickster_frontend_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", http_status=~"4xx|5xx"}[$__range])) > 0))

panels.title: Top routes
panels.description: The 25 busiest routes over the selected time range, by backend, method and configured path pattern (the route's path setting, not the raw URL). Req/s and Egress are averages over the range; 4xx and 5xx are shares of that route's responses; Mean latency excludes 1xx upgrades and CONNECT. Click a backend to filter this dashboard to it.

targets.expr: sum by (backend_name, provider, method, path) (rate(trickster_frontend_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}[$__range]))

(sum by (backend_name, provider, method, path) (rate(trickster_frontend_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", http_status="4xx"}[$__range])) or 0 * sum by (backend_name, provider, method, path) (rate(trickster_frontend_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}[$__range]))) / (sum by (backend_name, provider, method, path) (rate(trickster_frontend_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}[$__range])) > 0)

(sum by (backend_name, provider, method, path) (rate(trickster_frontend_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", http_status="5xx"}[$__range])) or 0 * sum by (backend_name, provider, method, path) (rate(trickster_frontend_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}[$__range]))) / (sum by (backend_name, provider, method, path) (rate(trickster_frontend_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}[$__range])) > 0)

sum by (backend_name, provider, method, path) (rate(trickster_frontend_requests_duration_seconds_sum{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", http_status!="1xx"}[$__range])) / (sum by (backend_name, provider, method, path) (rate(trickster_frontend_requests_duration_seconds_count{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", http_status!="1xx"}[$__range])) > 0)
sum by (backend_name, provider, method, path) (rate(trickster_frontend_written_bytes_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}[$__range]))

panels.title: Share of requests under 100 ms and 500 ms
panels.description: Share of front-end requests answered within 100 ms and within 500 ms, read straight from histogram bucket boundaries, so the values are exact. This is the most reliable latency signal here: a drop means more requests waiting on origins or slow clients. 1xx upgrades are excluded.

targets.expr: sum(rate(trickster_frontend_requests_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", http_status!="1xx", le="0.1"}[$__rate_interval])) / (sum(rate(trickster_frontend_requests_duration_seconds_count{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", http_status!="1xx"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0)

sum(rate(trickster_frontend_requests_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", http_status!="1xx", le="0.5"}[$__rate_interval])) / (sum(rate(trickster_frontend_requests_duration_seconds_count{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", http_status!="1xx"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0)

panels.title: Response time: mean and p50 / p90 / p99
panels.description: Mean (exact, sum / count) and estimated quantiles of front-end response time, excluding 1xx upgrades. The histogram's buckets are 50 ms, 100 ms, 500 ms, 1 s, 5 s, 10 s and 20 s, so anything faster than 50 ms (most cache hits) lands in the first bucket. Quantiles below 50 ms are interpolations and say nothing about real speed; above that they are only as precise as the bucket they fall in.

targets.expr: sum(rate(trickster_frontend_requests_duration_seconds_sum{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", http_status!="1xx"}[$__rate_interval])) / (sum(rate(trickster_frontend_requests_duration_seconds_count{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", http_status!="1xx"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0)
histogram_quantile(0.5, sum by (le) (rate(trickster_frontend_requests_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", http_status!="1xx"}[$__rate_interval])))
histogram_quantile(0.9, sum by (le) (rate(trickster_frontend_requests_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", http_status!="1xx"}[$__rate_interval])))
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(trickster_frontend_requests_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", http_status!="1xx"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Response time distribution
panels.description: Front-end requests per histogram bucket over time (1xx upgrades excluded); darker cells hold more requests. The histogram's buckets are 50 ms, 100 ms, 500 ms, 1 s, 5 s, 10 s and 20 s, so anything faster than 50 ms (most cache hits) lands in the first bucket. Mass moving into the 1 s and higher rows means origin fetches or large downloads are slowing down.

targets.expr: sum by (le) (increase(trickster_frontend_requests_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", http_status!="1xx"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Mean response time by backend
panels.description: Mean front-end response time (sum / count, exact) for the 10 slowest backends, excluding 1xx upgrades. An ALB's time includes its members' time: a merging ALB (tsm, nlm) waits for its slowest member, while a first-response ALB (fr, fgr) returns as soon as one member gives a usable answer. Backends serving large files or streams read high without being unhealthy.

targets.expr: topk(10, sum by (backend_name) (rate(trickster_frontend_requests_duration_seconds_sum{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", http_status!="1xx"}[$__rate_interval])) / (sum by (backend_name) (rate(trickster_frontend_requests_duration_seconds_count{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", http_status!="1xx"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0))

panels.title: Requests slower than 500 ms by backend
panels.description: Share of each backend's front-end requests that took longer than 500 ms, for the 10 worst backends. Exact (read from the 500 ms bucket boundary). Cache hits rarely exceed it, so a rising line usually means cache misses waiting on a slow origin; compare with the backend's hit ratio on the Caching dashboard.

targets.expr: topk(10, 1 - (sum by (backend_name) (rate(trickster_frontend_requests_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", http_status!="1xx", le="0.5"}[$__rate_interval])) / (sum by (backend_name) (rate(trickster_frontend_requests_duration_seconds_count{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", http_status!="1xx"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0)))

panels.title: Egress bytes/s by backend
panels.description: Response body bytes per second written to clients for the 10 busiest backends, after compression and before TLS (headers excluded). An ALB's bytes are counted under the ALB and again under the member that served them; mirror copies are counted under the mirror backend although no client receives them. Tunnels and long streams add their bytes when they close.

targets.expr: topk(10, sum by (backend_name) (rate(trickster_frontend_written_bytes_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Average response size by backend
panels.description: Average response body size (bytes written / requests) for the 10 backends with the largest responses. A sudden jump on a time series backend usually means clients asking for wider ranges or more series; a drop to near zero can mean error bodies replacing data.

targets.expr: topk(10, sum by (backend_name) (rate(trickster_frontend_written_bytes_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}[$__rate_interval])) / (sum by (backend_name) (rate(trickster_frontend_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0))

panels.title: Connections accepted, closed and failed
panels.description: New connections accepted, connections closed (any reason: client hang-up, idle timeout, drain) and failed accepts per second, across all metered TCP listeners. Accepted includes Prometheus scrapes and management calls. Failed (right axis) blips at reloads and restarts are listeners closing; a sustained rate usually means file-descriptor exhaustion. Closes of TLS connections are not counted.

targets.expr: sum(rate(trickster_proxy_accepted_connections_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval]))
sum(rate(trickster_proxy_closed_connections_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval]))
sum(rate(trickster_proxy_failed_connections_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Active connections vs connections_limit
panels.description: Open connections per instance, with the instance's connections_limit as a dashed line when one is set. At the limit, new connections queue in the accept backlog instead of being refused. TLS connections are never subtracted on close, so with HTTPS listeners the line climbs for the life of the process. With several limited listeners the limit line shows the one started last, and it keeps its value after a reload removes the limit.

targets.expr: sum by (instance) (trickster_proxy_active_connections{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"})
max by (instance) (trickster_proxy_max_connections{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"} > 0)

panels.title: Requests per new connection
panels.description: Front-end requests per newly accepted connection, per instance and ignoring Backend: a keep-alive and HTTP/2 reuse indicator. Near 1 means clients open a connection per request, which costs a TCP (and TLS) handshake each time. Approximate: ALB member sub-requests inflate the numerator, scrapes and non-HTTP listeners the denominator, and HTTP/3 requests use no TCP connection.

targets.expr: sum by (instance) (rate(trickster_frontend_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])) / (sum by (instance) (rate(trickster_proxy_accepted_connections_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0)

panels.title: Health probe latency p90 by backend
panels.description: 90th percentile duration of active health probes for the 10 slowest backends; only backends with a healthcheck interval > 0 are probed (typically ALB pool members). Passing and failing probes are mixed, so a jump to the probe timeout means probes are timing out; HTTP probes stop the clock at the response headers. Buckets run from 5 ms to 10 s. Backends without an HTTP route, such as SQL wire backends, show only when Backend is All.

links.title: Load Balancing: pool and member health

targets.expr: topk(10, histogram_quantile(0.9, sum by (le, backend_name) (rate(trickster_healthcheck_probe_latency_seconds_bucket{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}[$__rate_interval]))))

panels.title: Health probes by backend
panels.description: Per backend over the selected range: probes per minute, summed across instances (60 / interval per instance while probing runs; 0 or missing means it stopped), mean probe time (exact) and p90 / p99 estimated from buckets starting at 5 ms. Probe results (pass or fail) are not in this metric; pool health per member is on the Load Balancing dashboard.

links.title: Load Balancing: pool and member health

targets.expr: sum by (backend_name) (rate(trickster_healthcheck_probe_latency_seconds_count{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}[$__range])) * 60

sum by (backend_name) (rate(trickster_healthcheck_probe_latency_seconds_sum{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}[$__range])) / (sum by (backend_name) (rate(trickster_healthcheck_probe_latency_seconds_count{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}[$__range])) > 0)
histogram_quantile(0.9, sum by (le, backend_name) (rate(trickster_healthcheck_probe_latency_seconds_bucket{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}[$__range])))
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, backend_name) (rate(trickster_healthcheck_probe_latency_seconds_bucket{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}[$__range])))

panels.title: Upstream retries
panels.description: Upstream retry attempts over the selected range. Each extra attempt counts, so a request retried twice adds two; retries refused by the path's retry budget are not counted. Reads 0 when no path has a retry block.

targets.expr: sum(increase(trickster_proxy_upstream_retries_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}[$__range])) or vector(0)

panels.title: Mirror copies dropped
panels.description: Mirror copies dropped over the selected range, because the mirror's max_in_flight bound was reached or the request body could not be buffered. Clients are never affected; the mirror backend just sees less traffic. Reads 'not configured' when no selected backend has a path with a mirrors list.

targets.expr: sum(increase(trickster_proxy_mirror_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", result="dropped"}[$__range])) or vector(-1)

panels.title: SRV degraded lookups
panels.description: SRV lookups over the selected range that served a stale answer after a failed refresh, a cached negative answer (NXDOMAIN, empty or failed), or failed outright. Stale keeps traffic flowing; negative and error mean dials found nothing to connect to. Reads 'not configured' when no selected backend uses SRV origin resolution.

targets.expr: sum(increase(trickster_proxy_origin_srv_lookups_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", result=~"stale|negative|error"}[$__range])) or vector(-1)

panels.title: SigV4 signing failures
panels.description: Requests over the selected range that could not be SigV4-signed and so were never sent; clients received errors. Usually missing or unreadable AWS credentials. Reads 0 without a sigv4 block.

targets.expr: sum(increase(trickster_proxy_sigv4_events_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", event="sign_failure"}[$__range])) or vector(0)

panels.title: Upstream retries/s by backend and path
panels.description: Extra upstream attempts per second under each path's retry policy, for the 10 busiest backend / path pairs. A retry follows a connection failure or a response code listed in the policy's codes; sustained retries mean an unhealthy origin. Retries refused by the path's retry budget are not counted, so during an outage the line is capped by the budget.

targets.expr: topk(10, sum by (backend_name, path) (rate(trickster_proxy_upstream_retries_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Retries per request by backend and path
panels.description: Upstream retry attempts divided by front-end requests on the same backend and configured path. Can exceed 100% when requests are retried more than once. A path with no line has never retried since Trickster started.

targets.expr: topk(10, sum by (backend_name, path) (rate(trickster_proxy_upstream_retries_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}[$__rate_interval])) / on (backend_name, path) (sum by (backend_name, path) (rate(trickster_frontend_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0))

panels.title: Mirror copies/s by result
panels.description: Request copies per second sent to each mirror backend, by result. sent is counted when the mirror backend finishes serving the copy, so a slow mirror lags; dropped means the max_in_flight bound (64 by default) was reached or the body could not be buffered. Copies also appear in the front-end request panels under the mirror backend's name.

targets.expr: sum by (mirror_backend, result) (rate(trickster_proxy_mirror_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Mirror drop ratio by mirror backend
panels.description: Share of copies destined for each mirror backend that were dropped. A steady non-zero ratio means the mirror is too slow for its share of traffic; raise max_in_flight or lower percent. The client's own response is never affected.

targets.expr: sum by (mirror_backend) (rate(trickster_proxy_mirror_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", result="dropped"}[$__rate_interval])) / (sum by (mirror_backend) (rate(trickster_proxy_mirror_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0)

panels.title: SRV lookups/s by result
panels.description: SRV lookups per second by result, one per new upstream connection: hit (cached answer), miss (fresh lookup), stale (failed refresh, last good answer served), negative (cached NXDOMAIN, empty or failed answer), error. The rate tracks connection churn, not request volume, so it can be near zero under heavy keep-alive traffic.

targets.expr: sum by (result) (rate(trickster_proxy_origin_srv_lookups_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: SRV degraded-lookup ratio by backend
panels.description: Share of each backend's SRV lookups that were stale, negative or errors. Brief stale periods ride out DNS hiccups; sustained negative or error results mean the SRV name has nothing dialable and upstream requests are failing.

targets.expr: sum by (backend_name) (rate(trickster_proxy_origin_srv_lookups_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", result=~"stale|negative|error"}[$__rate_interval])) / (sum by (backend_name) (rate(trickster_proxy_origin_srv_lookups_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0)

panels.title: SRV dial attempts/s by tier and result
panels.description: TCP dial attempts to SRV targets per second by priority tier and result. Tier is the position among the answer's priority groups (0 = preferred), not the SRV priority value. One dial can make several attempts: failures in tier 0 followed by success in tier 1 is a failover.

targets.expr: sum by (tier, result) (rate(trickster_proxy_origin_srv_dial_attempts_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: SRV dials leaving the preferred tier
panels.description: Share of each backend's SRV dial attempts made to tier 1 or lower-priority targets. Above zero means preferred targets are failing or unreachable and traffic is failing over. A backend with no line has only ever dialed tier 0.

targets.expr: sum by (backend_name) (rate(trickster_proxy_origin_srv_dial_attempts_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", tier!="0"}[$__rate_interval])) / (sum by (backend_name) (rate(trickster_proxy_origin_srv_dial_attempts_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0)

panels.title: SigV4 events by backend
panels.description: SigV4 events per minute on backends with a sigv4 block (for example Amazon Managed Prometheus or CloudWatch). credentials_retry: the origin rejected expiring credentials and the request was resent with refreshed ones, normal around credential rotation. sign_failure: the request could not be signed and was not sent.

targets.expr: sum by (backend_name, event) (rate(trickster_proxy_sigv4_events_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}[$__rate_interval])) * 60
